title: Shared owner-authored document editor
goal: Consolidate and harden the current scene/note/material owner-authored editing flow into a shared editor pattern that preserves exact user-authored content and consistent selection/load/save/dirty-state behavior without generated prose, extraction, summaries, model calls, or memory/canon mutation.
why_now: PHASE7-IMPL-005 completed note/material storage, routes, API helpers, and a minimal navigation/display shell. The workspace now has scenes, notes, and materials available in the frontend, but the editor state and handlers remain duplicated and need a shared owner-authored document contract before later workspace pages build on them.

include: Define a conservative PHASE7-IMPL-006 child sequence.
Prepare status and roadmap records before runtime implementation begins.
Identify PHASE7-IMPL-006-T002 as the next source-level contract/test child.
exclude: Generated prose, rewriting, summaries, extraction, semantic search, model/Ollama calls, OMI promotion, memory/canon mutation, metadata editing UI, Dramatica analysis, training data, JSONL, dataset artifacts, package changes, app servers, frontend builds, and runtime project fixture writes.

quality_notes: Roadmap index and implementation status are primary authority for task identity and active frontier.
Direct reads of named source files were used for implementation-surface inventory.
Existing frontend tests are source-level guards and do not substitute for browser/manual validation.
No CCE, Graphify, Repomix, AI Context generation, MCP tools, LeanCTX, or broad discovery were run.

frontend.notes: Owns separate scene, note, and material state groups plus selectedDocumentType; load/save and dirty-state logic is duplicated across document types.
Accepts documentType, selectedDocumentId, generic documentError, and body content props; uses TipTap and currently provides document-type labels.
Renders scene, note, and material lists; normalizes display labels; active highlighting uses activeDocumentType plus selected IDs.
Exposes scene, note, and material body helpers; note/material metadata helpers exist but are not used by the minimal shell.

backend.notes: Provides scene and note/material body routes; PHASE7-IMPL-006 is expected to avoid backend route changes unless a later narrow bug fix is scoped.
Provides safe body/metadata storage helpers for scenes, notes, and materials.

tests.notes: Primary source-level regression target for shared editor contract work.

child_tasks.title: Shared owner-authored document editor inventory and child-task plan
Shared document state contract and source-level tests
scope: Define source-level expectations for active document type, document ID, content, dirty state, loading state, save status, and errors.
Add source-level regression checks before runtime refactor.
Avoid runtime implementation unless explicitly scoped by T002.

child_tasks.title: Editor component prop cleanup and behavior parity

acceptance_criteria: Scene, note, and material body editing share a documented frontend contract.
Selection/load/save behavior uses document IDs rather than display titles.
Body saves preserve exact owner-authored content and do not inject metadata.
Dirty-state, save-status, loading-state, and error handling are consistent across document types.
Project switching remains guarded when owner-authored document content has unsaved changes.
Existing scene behavior and PHASE7-IMPL-005 note/material shell behavior remain stable.

No generated prose, summaries, extraction, model/Ollama calls, OMI/canon/memory mutation, Dramatica analysis, training/JSONL/dataset work, package changes, app servers, frontend builds, or runtime project fixture writes are introduced.

safety_notes: Editor body content is owner-authored or owner-provided content.
Saving editor body content must not be blocked as AI prose generation.
AI output must never be inserted into scene, note, or material body content.
Future analysis/extraction must remain separate from editor body content and produce diagnostics or candidates only.
deferred_work: Metadata editing UI unless separately scoped.
Extraction, summaries, semantic search, OMI promotion, memory/canon mutation, Dramatica analysis, model/Ollama calls, training/JSONL/dataset work, and runtime project fixture changes.
